channel.title: Plain Earnings — new reports
channel.description: New earnings reports explained in plain English, with interactive money-flow charts.

item.title: Moderna — Q3 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: Moderna swung back to a profit on 29% revenue growth, but the profit is thin and the cost cuts did as much work as the sales rebound — and the fat cash balance came from a $3 billion convertible-note raise, not from operations.

item.title: Microsoft — FY27 Q1 earnings, explained
item.description: Microsoft grew 19% to $92.3B on Azure's 48% surge, and customers have now committed $677B of future cloud spending — the AI boom is real, and so is the bill to build it.

item.title: Alphabet — Q3 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: Google's operating profit rose 30% and Cloud more than doubled — but an $8.7B paper loss on its stock holdings turned the bottom line down 24%.

item.title: Amazon — Q3 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: Amazon's operating profit jumped 61% as AWS accelerated to 39% growth — but net income slipped, because last year's quarter included a $9.5B one-off Anthropic gain, and free cash flow went deeply negative on AI data-center spending.

item.title: Meta Platforms — Q3 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: Meta's ads grew 26% to $64.6B, but a $9.9B legal settlement cut operating profit by more than a third — and the number to watch is the $7.40 it would have earned without it.

item.title: Berkshire Hathaway — Q3 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: Berkshire's operating profit slipped 5.8% as GEICO's claims costs jumped, but the real story is the $9.6 billion buyback — more than the whole first half combined — while the 28% drop in headline profit mostly reflects smaller stock-market gains than last year, not weaker businesses.

item.title: Nvidia — Q2 FY27 earnings, explained
item.description: Nvidia's revenue more than doubled to $96.2B on the Blackwell Ultra ramp — data centers are now 93% of the business — but $7.8B of the $59.7B profit came from gains on its stock portfolio, not from selling chips.

item.title: Apple — Q4 FY26 earnings, explained
item.description: Apple's September quarter set records — $114.5B in revenue, iPhone up 17% to $57.6B — with Services at an all-time high and a one-off tariff refund adding a point to the margin.

item.title: Microsoft — Q4 FY26 earnings, explained
item.description: Microsoft closed fiscal 2026 with $90B in revenue, Azure up 43% and past $100B for the year — and a $3.2B Anthropic gain flattered the bottom line.

item.title: NVIDIA — Q1 FY26 earnings, explained
item.description: Nvidia's revenue jumped 69% to $44.1B on AI data-center demand, but a $4.5B charge for H20 chips blocked from China cut gross margin to 60.5% — without it, earnings would have been $0.96 a share instead of $0.76.

item.title: Apple — Q3 FY25 earnings, explained
item.description: Apple set a June-quarter revenue record — $94.0B, up 10% — with iPhone up 13% to $44.6B and Services at an all-time high of $27.4B.

item.title: Microsoft — FY25 Q3 earnings, explained
item.description: Microsoft grew 13% to $70.1B as Azure jumped 33% and the cloud passed $42B — AI demand is lifting every part of the business, even while the data-center buildout pushes costs up faster than revenue.

item.title: CoreWeave — Q1 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: CoreWeave's revenue more than doubled to $2.1B and its backlog reached $99.4B, but $536M of net interest turned a $144M operating loss into a $740M net loss.

item.title: Arm Holdings — Q1 FY27 earnings, explained
item.description: Arm's revenue hit a record $1.29B, up 22%, with data center royalties more than doubling — but GAAP profit stayed thin at $270M, and nearly half of it came from gains on investments, not the chip business.

item.title: Amazon — Q1 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Amazon's sales rose 13% to $143.3B and operating income more than tripled to $15.3B as AWS reaccelerated to 17% growth and International turned profitable — and it kept $10.4B as profit even after a $2.0B paper loss on its Rivian stake.

item.title: Arm Holdings — Q4 FY26 earnings, explained
item.description: Arm closed fiscal 2026 with a record $1.49B quarter, up 20%, as licensing hit a record $819M — but GAAP profit of $313M was less than half the $641M non-GAAP figure, mostly because of $261M of share-based pay.

item.title: CoreWeave — Q4 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: CoreWeave's revenue more than doubled to $1.6B and its backlog reached $66.8B, but $388M of net interest turned an $89M operating loss into a $452M net loss.

item.title: NVIDIA — Q3 FY24 earnings, explained
item.description: Nvidia's revenue tripled to a record $18.1B as Data Center sales jumped 279% on AI demand — and it kept $9.2B as profit, about 51 cents of every dollar.

item.title: Apple — Q1 FY24 earnings, explained
item.description: Apple's sales grew 2% to $119.6B as Services set an all-time record and iPhone rose 6% — and EPS hit an all-time high of $2.18, with $33.9B kept as profit.

item.title: Alphabet — Q1 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Alphabet grew revenue 15% to $80.5B as Search rose 14% and Google Cloud jumped 28% — and it kept $23.7B as profit, helped by a $2.2B paper gain on its investment stakes.

item.title: Hims & Hers — Q3 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: Revenue jumped 49% as international sales more than quadrupled, but Hims & Hers swung to a $33 million loss as gross margin collapsed 17 points and spending on marketing, admin and acquisitions piled up — growth bought at the cost of profitability.

item.title: Rocket Lab — Q3 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: Rocket Lab posted a record $268 million quarter with its backlog up 52% to $3.6 billion, but it still lost $80 million as Neutron development spending outran revenue — and the balance sheet now holds $4.4 billion in cash after a $3.9 billion share sale to fund the Iridium deal.

item.title: Datadog — Q4 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Revenue grew 29% to $953 million and Datadog stayed profitable on a GAAP basis, but the GAAP operating margin was just 1% — stock-based pay is the wedge between the $9 million GAAP operating profit and $230 million non-GAAP.

item.title: Mastercard — Q4 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Net revenue rose 18% to $8.8 billion as cross-border spending jumped 14% and value-added services grew 26% — and Mastercard kept $4.1 billion as profit, a 46% net margin.

item.title: CoreWeave — Q3 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: CoreWeave's revenue nearly tripled to a record $3.66 billion and operating profit quadrupled, but the company still lost $709 million because $846 million of interest on its $47 billion debt pile swallowed the entire operating profit — and it is spending $9.4 billion a quarter on new data centers to keep growing.

item.title: Airbnb — Q4 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Airbnb's revenue grew 12% to $2.8B on its strongest bookings quarter of the year — 121.9 million nights and seats — but planned investments and about $90M of non-income tax charges pushed net income down to $341M, 12 cents of every revenue dollar.

item.title: Bank of America — Q4 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Bank of America's revenue rose 7% to $28.4B with net interest income up 10% to $15.8B, and net income grew 12% to $7.6B as EPS rose 18% to $0.98 — capping a year in which profit reached $30.5B.

item.title: Intel — Q4 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Intel's revenue fell 4% to $13.7B and it lost $333M, as a $671M tax bill — almost double its pre-tax profit — wiped out a modest operating profit, even though data-center sales grew 9%.

item.title: Block — Q4 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Block's gross profit jumped 24% to $2.9B as Cash App surged 33%, but a $234M paper loss on its bitcoin holdings held net income to just $116M.

item.title: Adobe — Q4 FY25 earnings, explained
item.description: Adobe closed FY2025 with record quarterly revenue of $6.19B, up 10%, and record operating cash flow of $3.16B, as subscriptions grew 12% and total ARR reached $25.20B.

item.title: Exxon Mobil — Q4 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: ExxonMobil's profit fell 15% to $6.5 billion as lower oil prices cut Upstream earnings nearly in half, but surging refining margins lifted Energy Products earnings to $3.4 billion and the company still returned $9.5 billion to shareholders.

item.title: UnitedHealth Group — Q4 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: UnitedHealth Group's revenue grew 12% to $113.2B, but a 92.4% medical care ratio and a $2.9 billion one-time charge left operating profit at just $0.4B and earnings at a penny a share.

item.title: Vylor — Q3 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: Vylor's first quarter as a standalone seed company was a $480 million loss, as a seasonally small third quarter collided with $99 million of spin-off costs and weather-hit volumes, even as prices rose 6% and full-year guidance was reaffirmed.

item.title: Moderna — Q4 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Moderna lost $826 million in Q4 as COVID vaccine sales fell 30%, but the loss narrowed from $1.1 billion a year ago because deep cost cuts — R&D down 31% — outpaced the revenue decline, and management now promises growth again in 2026.

item.title: Nu Holdings — Q3 2026 earnings, explained
item.description: Nu posted a record $1.09 billion profit as revenue grew 37% on an FX-neutral basis and the efficiency ratio hit a best-ever 19.3%, but credit is the price of that growth — expected credit losses jumped 71% and the 90+ day delinquency rate rose to 7.3% — even as the bank added 3.7 million customers and took its first steps beyond Latin America with launches in the U.S.

item.title: Arm Holdings — Q4 FY25 earnings, explained
item.description: Arm's revenue jumped 34% to a record $1,241M — its first quarter above $1 billion — as both license and royalty revenue set records, but a $290M loss on equity investments held GAAP net income to $210M, down 6% from a year ago.

item.title: Shopify — Q3 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Shopify grew revenue 32% to $2.8B and generated $507M of free cash flow, but paper losses on its equity investments cut net income to $264M even as operating income rose 21%.

item.title: Spotify — Q3 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Spotify grew revenue 7% to €4.3B (about $5.0B) as Premium subscribers hit 281 million, while a tax benefit and a paper gain on its Exchangeable Notes lifted net income to €899M — well above operating income of €582M.

item.title: Snowflake — Q2 FY26 earnings, explained
item.description: Snowflake's revenue grew 32% to $1.14B, with product revenue up 32% to $1.09B — but $436M of stock-based pay helped leave a GAAP operating loss of $340M and a net loss of $298M.

item.title: Cloudflare — Q3 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Cloudflare grew revenue 31% to $562M and nearly broke even on a GAAP basis — a net loss of just $1.3M — as $39.3M of mostly interest income offset a $37.5M operating loss, while existing customers expanded spending at a 119% retention rate.

item.title: Arm Holdings — Q3 FY25 earnings, explained
item.description: Arm's revenue rose 19% to a record $983M on record royalty revenue of $580M, and GAAP net income nearly tripled to $252M as a $39M gain on equity investments and a low 6.0% tax rate lifted the bottom line.

item.title: Shopify — Q2 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Shopify grew revenue 31% to $2.7B and generated $422M of free cash flow, while a $681M paper gain on equity investments lifted net income to $906M — far above the $338M earned excluding those investments.

item.title: Spotify — Q2 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Spotify grew revenue 10% to €4.2B (about $4.9B) and added 8 million paying subscribers, but a €421M paper loss on its Exchangeable Notes — the notes are worth more when the share price rises — swung the quarter to a net loss of €86M despite operating income of €406M.

item.title: Snowflake — Q1 FY26 earnings, explained
item.description: Snowflake's revenue grew 26% to $1.04B, with product revenue up 26% to $997M — but $409M of stock-based pay and a $106M office-exit impairment helped leave a GAAP operating loss of $447M and a net loss of $430M.

item.title: Cloudflare — Q2 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Cloudflare grew revenue 28% to $512M, crossing $2B in annualized revenue, but heavy stock-based compensation kept it GAAP-unprofitable with a $50.4M net loss, even as existing customers expanded spending at a 114% retention rate.

item.title: Intel — Q3 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Intel's revenue rose 3% to $13.7B and it reported $4.1B of net income attributable to Intel, but $5.5B of that came from selling a majority stake in Altera — without it, underlying profit was about $1.0B, and Foundry still lost $2.3B.

item.title: Arm Holdings — Q2 FY25 earnings, explained
item.description: Arm's revenue rose 5% to $844M, above the high end of guidance, on record second-quarter royalty revenue of $514M, and a $43M tax benefit lifted a thin $64M operating profit to $107M of net income.

item.title: Spotify — Q1 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Spotify grew revenue 15% to €4.19B (about $4.5B) and added 5 million paying subscribers, with operating income more than tripling to a record €509M — but a €180M paper loss on its Exchangeable Notes and a €103M tax bill held net income to €225M.

item.title: Shopify — Q1 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Shopify grew revenue 27% to $2.4B and more than doubled operating income to $203M, but a $1,021M paper loss on equity investments swung the bottom line to a $682M net loss — excluding those investments, net income was $226M.

item.title: Snowflake — Q4 FY25 earnings, explained
item.description: Snowflake's revenue grew 27% to $986.8M, with product revenue up 28% to $943.3M — but $449.1M of stock-based pay helped leave a GAAP operating loss of $386.7M and a net loss of $325.7M.

item.title: Cloudflare — Q1 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Cloudflare grew revenue 27% to $479M and signed the largest contract in its history, but heavy stock-based compensation kept it GAAP-unprofitable with a $38.5M net loss, even as free cash flow jumped to $52.9M.

item.title: Intel — Q2 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Intel lost $2.9 billion in the second quarter as $1.9 billion of restructuring charges and roughly $1 billion of impairments and one-time costs pushed its costs past flat revenue of $12.9 billion, and its chip factories alone lost $3.2 billion.

item.title: Arm Holdings — Q1 FY25 earnings, explained
item.description: Arm's revenue jumped 39% to a record $939M on record license revenue of $472M, and net income more than doubled to $223M as royalty revenue grew 17% on wider Armv9 adoption.

item.title: Shopify — Q4 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Shopify's biggest quarter yet: revenue grew 31% to $2.8B and operating income jumped 61% to $465M — but $835M of the $1.3B net income was a paper gain on equity investments, so the underlying profit was $458M.

item.title: Spotify — Q4 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Spotify grew revenue 16% to €4.24B (about $4.4B) and added a record 35 million monthly users, with operating income hitting a record €477M — capping its first full year of operating profit — and net income swinging to €367M from a €70M loss a year ago.

item.title: Snowflake — Q3 FY25 earnings, explained
item.description: Snowflake's revenue grew 28% to $942.1M, with product revenue up 29% to $900.3M — but $381.4M of stock-based pay helped leave a GAAP operating loss of $365.5M and a net loss of $327.9M.

item.title: Cloudflare — Q4 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Cloudflare grew revenue 27% to $460M and added a record number of million-dollar customers, but $98.4M of stock-based compensation kept it GAAP-unprofitable with a $12.8M net loss, even as operating cash flow hit $127.3M.

item.title: Intel — Q1 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Intel lost $887 million in the first quarter as flat revenue of $12.7 billion met a thinner 36.9% gross margin, and its chip factories alone lost $2.3 billion while a new CEO moved to cut costs and spending.

item.title: Home Depot — Q3 FY26 earnings, explained
item.description: Home Depot grew sales 4.9% with comparable sales up 2.2%, but the growth came from bigger tickets, not more shoppers — transactions fell — and margins slipped as the cost of goods grew faster than sales.

item.title: Disney — Q4 FY26 earnings, explained
item.description: Disney ended fiscal 2026 with a blowout fourth quarter — revenue up 16% and adjusted EPS up 59% — but roughly a third of the operating-profit growth came from a 53rd week that won't repeat, and the parks, not streaming, still deliver most of the profit.

item.title: Arm Holdings — Q4 FY24 earnings, explained
item.description: Arm's revenue jumped 47% to a record $928M on record royalty revenue of $514M, and net income surged to $224M from $3M a year ago — though most of the profit came from a $166M tax benefit, not from operations.

item.title: Shopify — Q3 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Shopify grew revenue 26% to $2.2B and more than doubled operating income to $283M — but $344M of the $828M net income was a paper gain on equity investments, so the underlying profit was $484M.

item.title: Spotify — Q3 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Spotify grew revenue 19% to €3.99B (about $4.5B) and hit record profitability — gross margin of 31.1% and operating income of €454M, both records — as 640 million monthly users and 252 million paying subscribers each grew double digits, swinging net income to €300M from €65M a year ago.

item.title: Snowflake — Q2 FY25 earnings, explained
item.description: Snowflake's revenue grew 29% to $868.8M, with product revenue up 30% to $829.3M — but $373.3M of stock-based pay helped leave a GAAP operating loss of $355.3M and a net loss of $317.8M.

item.title: Disney — Q3 FY26 earnings, explained
item.description: Disney grew revenue 7% to $25.2B and segment profit 21% — streaming and parks both delivered — but an $812M writedown on its A+E stake, and comparison against last year's one-off tax benefit, cut reported EPS to $1.51.

item.title: Arm Holdings — Q3 FY24 earnings, explained
item.description: Arm's revenue hit a record $824M, up 14% and above its own guidance, on record royalty revenue — but net income fell 52% to $87M as hiring and share-based pay pushed operating costs up 45%.

item.title: Shopify — Q2 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Shopify grew revenue 21% to $2.0B and returned to a $241M operating profit — but $120M of investment losses, including a $44M loss on its Flexport stake, held net income to $171M.

item.title: Spotify — Q2 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Spotify grew revenue 20% to €3.81B (about $4.1B) and posted a record quarter — gross margin of 29.2% and operating income of €266M, both records — as 626 million monthly users and 246 million paying subscribers each grew double digits, swinging net income to €274M from a €302M loss a year ago.

item.title: Snowflake — Q1 FY25 earnings, explained
item.description: Snowflake's revenue grew 33% to $828.7M, with product revenue up 34% to $789.6M — but $360.4M of stock-based pay helped leave a GAAP operating loss of $348.6M and a net loss of $317.8M.

item.title: Cloudflare — Q3 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Cloudflare grew revenue 28% to $430.1M and added a record 219 large customers, but $91.8M of stock-based compensation kept it GAAP-unprofitable with a $15.3M net loss, even as operating cash flow hit $104.7M.

item.title: Palo Alto Networks — Q1 FY27 earnings, explained
item.description: Palo Alto Networks grew revenue 39% to a record $3.44B and raised full-year guidance sharply, but GAAP operating profit fell 69% to $96M as the CyberArk acquisition flooded the income statement with amortization and stock compensation — and a one-time $457M tax benefit is what turned $25M of pre-tax profit into $482M of net income.

item.title: Walmart — Q3 FY27 earnings, explained
item.description: Walmart's sales grew 5.2% to $188.8B and operating profit rose 16% as eCommerce jumped 17% — but headline profit fell 19.5% because last year's quarter included a $2.1B gain on investments that flipped to a $0.3B loss.

item.title: Spotify — Q1 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Spotify grew revenue 20% to €3.64B (about $3.9B) and posted a record quarter — gross margin of 27.6% and operating income of €168M, both records — as 615 million monthly users and 239 million paying subscribers each grew double digits, swinging net income to €197M from a €225M loss a year ago.

item.title: Shopify — Q1 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Shopify grew revenue 23% to $1.9B and returned to an $86M operating profit — but a $373M paper loss on its investments swung the quarter to a $273M net loss.

item.title: Snowflake — Q4 FY24 earnings, explained
item.description: Snowflake's revenue grew 32% to $774.7M, with product revenue up 33% to $738.1M — but $320.3M of stock-based pay helped leave a GAAP operating loss of $275.5M and a net loss of $169.9M.

item.title: Intuit — Q1 FY27 earnings, explained
item.description: Intuit opened fiscal 2027 with revenue up 12% to $4.4B and GAAP operating income up 63% as QuickBooks Online grew 20% — but the bigger news is the deal to sell Mailchimp for $3.68B, and the tax-season quarters ahead, not this one, are where Intuit makes most of its money.

item.title: Shopify — Q4 2023 earnings, explained
item.description: Shopify swung to a $657M profit in Q4 as revenue grew 24% to $2.1B — and a $368M gain on its investments supplied more than half of the bottom line.

item.title: Spotify — Q4 2023 earnings, explained
item.description: Spotify grew revenue 16% to €3.67B (about $4.1B) and narrowed its operating loss to €75M as 602 million monthly users and 236 million paying subscribers each grew double digits — but €143M of efficiency charges kept the quarter in the red, with a net loss of €70M.

item.title: Snowflake — Q3 FY24 earnings, explained
item.description: Snowflake's revenue grew 32% to $734.2M, with product revenue up 34% to $698.5M — but $307.4M of stock-based pay helped leave a GAAP operating loss of $260.6M and a net loss of $214.7M.

item.title: Cloudflare — Q2 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Cloudflare grew revenue 30% to $401.0M and crossed $1.6 billion in annualized revenue, but $89.5M of stock-based compensation kept it GAAP-unprofitable with a $15.1M net loss, even as operating cash flow hit $74.8M.

item.title: Intel — Q4 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Intel's chip business earned $412 million from operations in the fourth quarter, but a $752 million tax bill — bigger than its $599 million of pre-tax income — turned that profit into a $153 million net loss.

item.title: Cloudflare — Q1 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Cloudflare grew revenue 30% to $378.6M and turned $73.6M of operating cash flow, but $76.7M of stock-based compensation and a $15.0M one-time compensation charge kept it GAAP-unprofitable with a $35.5M net loss.

item.title: Intel — Q3 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Intel lost $17.0 billion in the third quarter after $5.6 billion of restructuring and impairment charges and a $9.9 billion tax charge for writing down deferred tax assets overwhelmed $13.3 billion of revenue.

item.title: Qualcomm — Q4 FY25 earnings, explained
item.description: Qualcomm grew revenue 10% to $11.3B on record chip sales, but a $5.7B one-time tax charge turned the quarter into a $3.1B net loss — without it, the business earned about $2.6B.

item.title: Super Micro Computer — Q1 FY26 earnings, explained
item.description: Supermicro's sales fell 15.5% to $5.0B as big AI orders landed too late in the quarter to ship, and with gross margin down to 9.3%, net income dropped 60% to $168M.

item.title: Marvell Technology — Q2 FY26 earnings, explained
item.description: Marvell's revenue hit a record $2.01B, up 58% on AI data-center demand — and GAAP profit swung to $195M from a $193M loss a year ago.

item.title: Texas Instruments — Q3 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Texas Instruments grew revenue 14% to $4.74B as Analog sales rose 16%, and operating profit climbed 7% — though restructuring charges and a bigger tax bill held net income flat at $1.36B.

item.title: ServiceNow — Q3 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: ServiceNow grew revenue 22% to $3.4B, beat its own guidance on every topline and profitability metric, and pre-sold another $24.3B of future business — while GAAP profit rose 16% to $502M.

item.title: Palo Alto Networks — Q4 FY25 earnings, explained
item.description: Palo Alto Networks grew revenue 16% to $2.54B and Next-Gen Security ARR 32% to $5.6B, but GAAP net income fell 29% to $254M — operating profit more than doubled, yet a one-time tax charge from the new One Big Beautiful Bill tax law pushed the tax bill to $338M and swallowed the gain.

item.title: DoorDash — Q3 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: DoorDash's marketplace kept compounding — orders up 21%, the value of goods ordered up 25% to $25.0B — and net income rose 51% to $244M even after an $81M non-cash loss on the currency hedge for the Deliveroo deal.

item.title: Airbnb — Q3 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Airbnb's biggest Q3 yet: 133.6 million nights and seats booked drove revenue up 10% to $4.1B, and net income held at $1.4B — 34 cents of every revenue dollar — despite a $213M one-off tax charge.

item.title: CrowdStrike — Q2 FY26 earnings, explained
item.description: CrowdStrike grew revenue 21% to $1.17B and signed a record $221M of new subscription business, but stock pay, outage costs and a restructuring charge kept the quarter in the red — a $78M net loss — even as non-GAAP profit hit a record $237M.

item.title: Datadog — Q3 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Datadog grew revenue 28% to $886M and stayed net-profitable at $34M, but its core operations lost $6M on a GAAP basis — $201M of stock pay is the whole gap to its $207M non-GAAP operating profit.

item.title: CrowdStrike — Q3 FY27 earnings, explained
item.description: CrowdStrike posted its best quarter ever — record net new ARR of $419 million, record operating and free cash flow, and revenue up 28% — but the GAAP profit is essentially zero ($25 million on $1.58 billion of sales) because $372 million of stock-based compensation eats the entire operating profit, and the day's real news is the $43.9 billion all-stock deal to buy Zscaler.

item.title: Super Micro Computer — Q4 FY25 earnings, explained
item.description: Supermicro's sales rose 7.5% to $5.8B, but thinner margins and higher R&D spending cut profit by a third to $195M — even as the quarter generated $864M of operating cash.

item.title: Intel — Q2 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Intel lost $1.6 billion in the second quarter on $12.8 billion of revenue, then suspended its dividend and announced a $10 billion cost-cutting plan with more than 15% of jobs to go.

item.title: Marvell Technology — Q1 FY26 earnings, explained
item.description: Marvell's revenue hit a record $1.90B, up 63% on AI data-center demand — and GAAP profit swung to $178M from a $216M loss a year ago.

item.title: CrowdStrike — Q1 FY27 earnings, explained
item.description: CrowdStrike grew revenue 26% to $1.39B and signed a record $256M of net new subscriptions, but the core business still lost $31M — $318M of stock pay ate the operating profit — and investment gains plus interest on its cash pile flipped the quarter to a $46M profit, only $28M of which belonged to CrowdStrike shareholders.

item.title: Texas Instruments — Q2 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: Texas Instruments earned $1.30 billion on $4.45 billion of revenue as sales grew 16% on a broad recovery in industrial demand, with operating profit up 25%.

item.title: ServiceNow — Q2 2025 earnings, explained
item.description: ServiceNow grew revenue 22.5% to $3.22 billion, with subscription sales up 22.5% and $10.9 billion of revenue already contracted for the next twelve months.

item.title: Marvell Technology — Q4 FY25 earnings, explained
item.description: Marvell's revenue hit a record $1.82B, up 27% on AI data-center demand — and GAAP profit swung to $200M from a $393M loss a year ago.

item.title: Qualcomm — Q3 FY25 earnings, explained
item.description: Qualcomm grew revenue 10% to $10.4B as its car and connected-device chips hit records, while the phone chips that still pay most of the bills grew 7%.

item.title: Intel — Q1 2024 earnings, explained
item.description: Intel still lost money in the first quarter — $381 million attributable to Intel on $12.7 billion of revenue — but the loss shrank 86% from a year ago as PC chip sales jumped 31%.

item.title: Super Micro Computer — Q3 FY25 earnings, explained
item.description: Supermicro sold 19.5% more in the quarter, but its thin margins got thinner and profit fell by nearly three-quarters to $109 million as customers delayed big AI platform decisions.
